items.summary: This technical note documents a conditional mathematical correspondence between the static spatial kernel used in conventional electromagnetic potential theory and the fixed-source gravitational potential in Lisa Doumbouya’s Harmonic Physics programme. Under supplied three-dimensional Euclidean geometry, spherical symmetry and stated boundary conditions, the derivation gives the static Green function 1/(4πr). Applying the existing gravitational source normalization yields the potential −μ/r, whose radial derivative gives the inward acceleration −μ/r². The note distinguishes potential, field amplitude, intensity, acceleration and optical measurement conversion, keeping geometric normalization separate from the distance exponent. The optical phase-ruler results are reviewed alongside the GRACE-FO forward forecasts. Calibrated reconstruction using measured phase retained micrometre-scale agreement with processed microwave ranging, while some forward models produced much larger errors. These results do not establish exponential error growth or identify a unique physical cause. The correspondence uses established mathematics and remains conditional on the supplied geometry, source calibration and physical interpretation. It does not establish an electromagnetic mechanism of gravity or derive spatial geometry from foundational Phase. The note includes the analytical proof, assumptions, evidence boundaries and requirements for a subsequent physical test. No new experimental data are introduced.

items.summary: This working paper develops a relational Phase interpretation of black holes within the Harmonic Physics research programme, using general relativity, exact Kerr geometry and semiclassical black-hole thermodynamics as its physical baseline. It examines how phase organisation, temporal reference, observer accessibility and information persistence might relate to black-hole closure. Within the proposed framework, a phase-cycle is a closed relational structure that supports recurrence. Measured succession requires distinguishable relations and persistent records, while geometry and causal history are treated as observer-level reconstructions. The temporal-anchor hypothesis concerns a deeper terminal condition at which the parent domain loses the internally usable references needed to resolve further clocks and geometry. This proposed condition is kept distinct from the regular event horizon, across which local evolution continues. Observation is described through a joint observation relation among admitted source organisation, a physical channel and an observer-capable organisation. Source state, coupling and registered record retain separate roles; changes in accessibility may alter registration while the source organisation persists. The paper consolidates three bounded mathematical findings: exact Kerr ingoing and outgoing endpoints can have opposite trapped and anti-trapped orientations with the same mass and spin parameters; spherical source/exterior matching leaves the transition law undetermined; and a leading slow-rotation calculation permits the same sign of angular momentum in closing and opening configurations. These results establish compatibility within the stated geometric constructions. A physical transition mechanism remains to be derived. Black-to-white-hole models provide external theoretical comparisons. Return to the original exterior and the opening of a daughter phase are treated as distinct hypotheses, each requiring an appropriate causal structure, state map and conservation accounting. The remaining requirements include an invariant parent-relative terminal criterion, a physical Phase-to-boundary map, transition dynamics, information and entropy accounting, and a stable nonperturbative rotating completion. The paper remains a developing theoretical interpretation supported by standard-geometry comparisons and bounded symbolic checks. It does not establish a physical black-to-white transition, information recovery through evaporation or a daughter universe. Version 2.3, dated 17 October 2026, updates observation and self-nesting terminology, clarifies geodesic incompleteness and fixed-angular-momentum assumptions, and refreshes the references. The existing displayed equations and reported test results are retained. keywords: Phase Theory; black holes; event horizons; geodesic incompleteness; relational time; phase contraction; information accessibility; singularity; white holes; quantum gravity.

items.summary: This release provides the data and code supporting a simulation-only study of reference-assisted radiofrequency fracture sensing under anatomical domain shift. It includes 5,580 corrected noise-free RF acquisitions, 356,400 feature rows from 20 independent noise repetitions, model predictions, calibration outputs and paired H2 statistical analyses. MATLAB and Python source code, fixed analysis specifications, figure-generation code and provenance records are included. The materials support reproducible evaluation of independent healthy references and source-locked decision thresholds across five idealised anatomical locations. All data are simulated and do not establish clinical diagnostic accuracy.
items.title: Data and Code for Machine Learning Based Reference Assisted Signal Recovery Under Anatomical Domain Shift in Simulated Radiofrequency Fracture Sensing

The key comparator is an equal-budget experiment: fixed-field sequences, microscope-assisted manual control, externally tracked predictive control and candidate fused navigation are evaluated under matched total energy, information access, geometry, time, collision limits and recovery obligations. The manuscript emphasizes blind targets, flow reversal, sensor dropouts, wall adhesion, correlated observations, full-system power accounting, censored failures and post-mission retrieval. A mission arriving at its target but leaving an unrecovered device is not counted as a fully closed success. This work is a hypothesis-generating Research Atlas v1.0, not an experimental report or a validated medical technology. External magnetic, acoustic, optical and microscope infrastructure must be disclosed; no in-vivo or clinical competence is inferred from bench-top movement. Foundational DOI-linked literature provides context, not proof of the proposed integrated system. items.summary: R scripts and aggregate tables that reproduce every number, table and figure in the article What a national health information system measures: a cross-sectional analysis of respiratory syncytial virus records in Bulgaria, 2022–2026 (Folia Medica, manuscript 215603) and its supplementary files. The package contains the reconstruction ledger of the Ministry of Health release of Bulgarian National Health Information System (NHIS) records for ICD-10 J21.0, J12.1, J20.5 and B97.4; exclusion and validation counts; the 110 distinct laboratory result values (109 text strings and the empty text field of numeric results) with their assigned RSV class and the rule that fired; a script that rebuilds the hospitalisation episodes from the released worksheet; annual population denominators at national and district level (National Statistical Institute table 206/649, population on 31 December 2022–2025); the aggregate model input (year × age × sex cases and person-years, with and without Sliven); model output and diagnostics; and the article figures. Aggregate data only. No record-level rows, identifiers or dates of birth are included; the record-level extract can be requested from the Bulgarian Ministry of Health under the Access to Public Information Act. See README.md for the file map, data sources, disclosure control and how to re-run the pipeline. Tables and figures: CC BY 4.0; R scripts: MIT licence.
items.title: Reproducibility package (R scripts and aggregate tables) for: What a national health information system measures: a cross-sectional analysis of respiratory syncytial virus records in Bulgaria, 2022–2026

Keys, credentials, executables, cloud administration records and manuscript/LaTeX source are excluded. Restrictions and provenance limits are documented. The files are per-unit derived counts of the 3,687 cohort-A accounts and the cohort-B identities, with random identifiers (marker dates reduced to the month; no account names, e-mail addresses, repository names, commit SHAs or commit times). Placed by python3 reproduce.py --level2 <folder> of the Level-1 package (version 1.0.3), they recompute the registered aggregates and the exploratory aggregates that do not require the raw commit logs, including rates, transitions, paired contrasts, random-exclusion benchmarks and bootstrap intervals; on Python 3.10.12 with numpy 2.2.6 (Linux, aarch64) and on Python 3.13.16 with numpy 2.5.3 (Linux, x86_64) every regenerated result agreed with the reported one (numerical values within 1e-9, text files identical apart from line endings). Access is restricted because cohort-B rows keep the positions of their repositories in the public sampling order, which the registered repository-cluster bootstrap needs. Access is granted to researchers who state their name, affiliation and purpose and who agree to use the files only to verify, reproduce or extend the analyses of the article, not to redistribute the files or per-unit derivatives, not to attempt any re-identification or linkage to public commit histories or accounts, to store the files securely and delete them when the work is complete, and to cite the article and both archives (ACCESS.md). The public Level-1 archive with the programs, tests and aggregate results is https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23226958 (all versions; version 1.0.3, cited in the manuscript: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23430269). Changes in 1.0.1: two files with the per-identity counts of the exploratory published-measure analysis (file-based churn, cohort B; Supplementary Section S13 of the article) were added, re-keyed like the other cohort-B files; every file of version 1.0.0 is unchanged. The files are per-unit derived counts of the 3,687 cohort-A accounts and the cohort-B identities, with random identifiers (marker dates reduced to the month; no account names, e-mail addresses, repository names, commit SHAs or commit times). Placed by python3 reproduce.py --level2 <folder> of the Level-1 package (version 1.0.3), they recompute the registered aggregates and the exploratory aggregates that do not require the raw commit logs, including rates, transitions, paired contrasts, random-exclusion benchmarks and bootstrap intervals; on Python 3.10.12 with numpy 2.2.6 (Linux, aarch64) and on Python 3.13.16 with numpy 2.5.3 (Linux, x86_64) every regenerated result agreed with the reported one (numerical values within 1e-9, text files identical apart from line endings). Access is restricted because cohort-B rows keep the positions of their repositories in the public sampling order, which the registered repository-cluster bootstrap needs. Access is granted to researchers who state their name, affiliation and purpose and who agree to use the files only to verify, reproduce or extend the analyses of the article, not to redistribute the files or per-unit derivatives, not to attempt any re-identification or linkage to public commit histories or accounts, to store the files securely and delete them when the work is complete, and to cite the article and both archives (ACCESS.md). Reviewers of the article receive an access link through the editor.

items.summary: We have presented a mathematically closed, comprehensive foundation for the C861 discrete spectral benchmark. By establishing the exact rank-two projector geometry, resolving Dirichlet sum cancellations, providing constructive proofs for linear B-spline KAN operator reproduction, and formalizing the Lyapunov convergence of Dense Associative Memory on spherical manifolds, this framework eliminates ambiguities in evaluating learned physical operators. Furthermore, the spectral interlacing analysis of the CN → PN structural homotopy equips the scientific machine learning community with a tool to distinguish authentic topological sensitivity from numerical discretization artifacts.
items.title: Exact Discrete Spectral Invariants as a Falsification Baseline for Learned Operator

items.summary: AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC NAVIGATION AND MISSION OBSERVABILITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation Research Flagship 01 | NANO/MICRO ROBOTICS, POWER & MISSION ENDURANCE Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli This research atlas asks a difficult engineering question: when low-Reynolds-number microfluidic flows, Brownian orientation noise, boundary adhesion, external field actuation and incomplete sensing all influence a micro/nanorobot, what would justify calling its behavior autonomous navigation rather than externally assisted motion? The volume treats navigation as an auditable, bounded mission instead of an attractive trajectory. It develops a five-layer program spanning stochastic hydrodynamics, instrument and actuation provenance, uncertainty-calibrated belief-state estimation, blinded microfluidic challenges and independent requalification. Thirty linked mathematical stations differentiate physical relations, information-theoretic functionals and proposed navigation utility measures, with assumptions, dimensions and possible falsifiers. Eighty-two research chapters each open with a core mathematical relation, followed by five independent single-page research sections. Two hundred detailed Research Gates describe decisive comparisons, confounding explanations, evidence requirements, failure conditions and successor handoff artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos offer revisionable research prototypes rather than predetermined conclusions. The key comparator is an equal-budget experiment: fixed-field sequences, microscope-assisted manual control, externally tracked predictive control and candidate fused navigation are evaluated under matched total energy, information access, geometry, time, collision limits and recovery obligations. The manuscript emphasizes blind targets, flow reversal, sensor dropouts, wall adhesion, correlated observations, full-system power accounting, censored failures and post-mission retrieval. A mission arriving at its target but leaving an unrecovered device is not counted as a fully closed success. This work is a hypothesis-generating Research Atlas v1.0, not an experimental report or a validated medical technology. External magnetic, acoustic, optical and microscope infrastructure must be disclosed; no in-vivo or clinical competence is inferred from bench-top movement. Foundational DOI-linked literature provides context, not proof of the proposed integrated system. Every major claim is designed to be revised, rejected or reconstructed by a successor team using raw evidence and pre-registered falsification rules. items.summary: Multi-agent path finding (MAPF) solvers are evaluated on the schedules they produce, not on how well those schedules can be executed. Specifically, continuous-time optimal solvers can achieve even lower cost than their discrete counterparts by scheduling agents with near-zero temporal/spatial separation, and by exploiting graphs with higher connectedness; however, such schedules may prove hard to execute under a realistic controller. We integrate AOC-CBS, an anytime-optimal continuous-time MAPF solver, into a fleet coordination framework in which each agent tracks its timed path using model predictive control, and we evaluate the resulting system on congested MovingAI benchmark instances with 21 to 40 agents. Without intervention, only a fraction of the instances complete execution. We then apply T-robustness by adding a time-margin, i.e., a minimum temporal gap between agents at shared locations, as well as spatial inflation of the agent footprint. Increasing either margin raises execution success, for a relatively small increase in the schedule's sum-of-costs; it also improves how closely agents adhere to the schedule: when tracking each agent's position throughout execution and comparing it against the position it should occupy according to the schedule, the mean discrepancy falls significantly as the margin increases. In general, the two margins have different effects; temporal margin decreases deviation, giving the controller room to stay on schedule. Spatial margin affects deviation less and instead increases the clearance between agents, so that the same deviation no longer leads to a blocking stall. They are nonetheless substitutes rather than complements: spatial inflation is almost free in schedule cost, but its effect on execution success is small and does not compound with a temporal margin already in place.
items.title: The Cost of Executability: Temporal Margins for Continuous-Time Multi-Agent Path Finding under Closed-Loop Control

items.summary: NANOROBOTIC CARGO TRANSPORT AND MICROSCALE MANIPULATION INTEGRITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation DOI Fission Research Flagship 02 | Starli Active Nanosystems Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli | Research Atlas v1.0 (October 2026) How can a micro/nanorobotic carrier demonstrate that the object arriving at a designated target is the same intact cargo that was originally loaded, that it was completely and correctly released, and that the carrier or its residues have been accounted for? This English-language research atlas converts cargo-delivery and micromanipulation demonstrations into a falsifiable end-to-end mission-integrity problem. The research develops a five-layer architecture for source identity and material tolerance, microscale contact mechanics, independently observable mission-state transitions, adversarial fault injection, and blind cross-platform requalification. Thirty mathematically distinct derivation stations connect probabilistic joint-task qualification to chemical mass balance, optical-label dissociation, surface adsorption, force-dependent detachment, microcontact mechanics, drag, kinetic release, spatial uncertainty, carryover contamination, whole-facility energy accounting, missing-fate bounds and hard safety vetoes. Eighty-two chapters each have a dedicated core-equation opening and five separate research sections. Two hundred Research Gates propose independent comparisons, physical perturbations, competing explanations, measurable failure criteria and reproducibility artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos outline candidate systems that future investigators are invited to overturn, repair or rebuild. A machine-readable research atlas and formula-gate-DOI index enable AI-assisted comparison and future research reuse. The central endpoint is a correlated joint event: correct cargo identity and integrity, correct target, independently confirmed release, and verified carrier retrieval or authorized terminal disposition. The manuscript insists on counting every initiated mission rather than multiplying attractive substep success rates. It also distinguishes visible fluorescence from chemically intact cargo, externally actuated manipulation from on-board autonomy, and destination arrival from complete task closure. Strong benchmarks include optical tweezers, established magnetic-bead handling, microfluidic conveyance and conventional microgrippers under matched task difficulty, time and whole-facility energy use. Research status: This is a hypothesis-generating, nonclinical experimental-design atlas; it reports no newly conducted cargo experiments, clinical performance or proven integrated device. Foundational and recent DOI-identified publications provide engineering context but do not validate its new claims. The 200 Gates are open problems, not accomplished results. The actual text length and layout follow the substance of individual chapters rather than an artificially enforced 100,000-word count. items.summary: EHR2Trace converts local hospital EHR extracts (delimited text and spreadsheets) into OMOP CDM 5.4 and MEDS. The two targets are derived independently from a single canonical layer rather than one from the other, every published row carries a link back to the source rows it came from, and fifty-five checks encode the properties a conversion must satisfy before it can be used as training data, including the leakage failures that are invisible to schema validation. Where the data does not answer a question, the converter blocks and says so instead of substituting a default. Companion paper: EHR2Trace: Auditable EHR Data Infrastructure for Patient World Models and Clinical Agents (arXiv:2609.38193).
items.title: EHR2Trace: a deterministic converter from local EHR exports to OMOP CDM 5.4 and MEDS, with row-level lineage

items.summary: Safe multi-agent coordination typically assumes what real-world, deployed, resource-constrained robots cannot provide: continuous, perfect state sharing. Robust control strategies must be complemented with robust communication strategies to deliver resilient deployments. In this work, we propose a unified control/communication strategy that provides safe control to guarantee inter-agent safety under intermittent communication and demonstrate its effectiveness in a pursuit-evasion scenario. Each agent computes the reachable set of neighboring agents based on the last state information received, then solves for a safe control input based on control barrier functions to ensure agents avoid collision. We prove that inter-agent collision avoidance is guaranteed provided communication staleness remains bounded. As the reachable set inflates between state transmissions, each agent reasons about when to preemptively transmit its state information to neighboring agents based on novel metrics characterizing uncertainty risk and kinematic risk. We implement and simulate a variety of pursuit-evasion scenarios and show that preemptive communication reduces messages by 77.5% compared to periodic and event-triggered baselines with zero collisions.
items.title: Robust Multi-Agent Pursuit with Preemptive Communication via Reachability-Based Control Barrier Functions

items.summary: Chlorine-based disinfectants are standard for environmental-surface disinfection in healthcare facilities, yet their reaction with organic residues generates disinfection by-products (DBPs) whose occurrence, levels, and occupational relevance on hospital surfaces remain uncharacterized. Key gaps are the lack of a validated method and baseline data, the unresolved origin of surface N-nitrosamines, and the unknown influence of chlorine, temperature, humidity, and pre-cleaning on the surface DBP signal. We developed an isotope-dilution wipe-sampling, solid-phase extraction, and ultra-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) method for eight priority DBPs, applied it to 125 wipe samples from five departments across three campuses of a tertiary hospital in Wenzhou, and complemented field work with stainless-steel coupon experiments. Validation gave r ≥ 0.999, detection limits of 0.8–3.8 pg/cm², and recoveries of 78.4%–96.8%; field detection and quantification frequencies were 87.2% (95% CI 80.2–92.0%) and 69.6% (95% CI 61.1–77.0%), with operating rooms showing the highest total load (Kruskal–Wallis H(4) = 27.86, P < 0.001) though no pairwise contrast survived Bonferroni correction. In coupon experiments the net signal rose with chlorine and temperature but not humidity, with an unexplained chlorine-dependent increment (≈55% at 2000 mg/L) reflecting analytical signal behavior rather than verified formation chemistry, and pre-cleaning reduced haloacetic acids and chlorophenols by 35–55% but N-nitrosamines by only 3–9%. These results provide the first isotope-dilution baseline of DBP loads on healthcare surfaces, a reproducible monitoring method, and occurrence data for revising disinfection and occupational-hygiene standards, and they identify precursor-controlled formation experiments, biological monitoring, and direct testing of medical rubber as next steps.
tags: disinfection by-products; healthcare environmental surface; ultra-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry; wipe sampling; N-nitrosamines; occupational exposure
items.title: Determination of Chlorination Disinfection By-products on Healthcare Environmental Surfaces by Ultra-Performance Liquid Chromatography–Tandem Mass Spectrometry

items.summary: Post-Soviet states have spent three decades rebuilding the civic curriculum around national rather than supranational loyalties, yet claims that modernized patriotic education changes what students know and value seldom face controlled scrutiny. This study evaluates a convergent model that couples national heritage content with interactive methods, digital gamification, STEAM-linked projects, and the weekly Kelajak Soati (Future Hour) curriculum in Uzbek general secondary schools. A three-stage quasi-experiment (ascertaining, 2022-2023; formative, 2023-2024; summative, 2024-2025) enrolled 1,192 students in ten schools across Tashkent, Fergana, and Navoiy, allocated to experimental (n = 594) and control (n = 598) conditions. Groups were equivalent at baseline (M = 3.52 vs. 3.53 on a three-level scale scored 3-5; t = −0.12, p = .90; χ 2 (2) = 0.40, p = .82). Change concentrated at the lower threshold: the share of experimental students at the Low level fell from 58.4% to 23.9% while the Medium level rose from 30.8% to 60.6%; the control distribution did not move. Effects replicated in every region (d = 0.56-0.65), and net-of-baseline gains were as large in the rural Fergana district as in Navoiy. The model reliably converts civic disengagement into baseline civic literacy; whether it fosters constructive rather than conformist attachment remains untested. Implications for national scale-up and its evaluation are discussed.
